title: Match records, part 2: a random player number after a yes, sessions, progress and a test bucket
problem: Nameless records cannot say that two games were played by the same player, so return, sessions, progression and "do better players win more" cannot be measured (REP-154).
scope: A one-time question on Home after a first game: "Help improve the game?" Yes or No thanks; until a yes no number exists

On yes: 16 random hex digits made and kept on the phone, sent with each match record together with a random session number, games started this session, the install day, a test bucket (a or b), stall level, league stage and looks unlocked
One line per app start for a player who said yes (POST /api/s), kept with the records
Settings: "Link my games" (off removes the number from the phone) and "Forget my data" (deletes every record and session line of the number on the server, and the number on the phone)
The reader prints players, games per player, return on a later day by first mode, levels and buckets
The privacy page's new section "A player number (only if you say yes)"
exclusions: No name, account ID or phone ID is ever linked to the number
No experiment yet: the two buckets play the same game
Online records carry no player number

acceptance.text: npm run verify, with tests: no number before a yes; a No leaves none; the number rides on a record; Forget my data removes it and calls the server
acceptance.evidence: 2026-11-28: npm run verify on the branch: 139 test files, 1445 tests passed, build OK (tests/match-records.test.ts: no number before a yes, rides on the record, Forget my data)

acceptance.text: On a local game server: a session line is stored; Forget my data deletes the number's record and session line
acceptance.evidence: 2026-11-28, local game server: a session line was stored; the forget route deleted the number's 2 rows

acceptance.text: The question and the Settings switches seen on a phone-sized screen
acceptance.evidence: The Settings screen was seen in a screenshot; the one-time question on Home was not
